pr_title: udev: don't name interfaces after laptop dock passthrough MAC addresses
pr_body:
Let's automatically suppress generation of "enx" names for network interfaces, if a system is configured to "clone" MAC addresses from internal network interfaces onto laptop dock interfaces.

In such a scenario lock MAC addresses are not uniquely assigned to local network interfaces, hence simply suppress any such naming schemes comprehensively.

Fixes: #33104

issue_context.title: Failed to rename network interface on docking ethernet (cloned MAC)
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

256~rc3

### Used distribution

Debian unstable

### Linux kernel version used

6.9.3

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

_No response_

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

Patch 0f5a529217f1327f020ab54deed09e6fae1f1fef added "mac"  to alternatives name policy in network/99-default.link.

This seems to be causing problem on my Lenovo dock with ethernet iterface that has cloned MAC from notebook (standard option in bios).

In normal situation, I get two interfaces: enp0s* (notebook) / enx00* (dock) with the same MAC.
(eth names are redacted, they do not contain * :)

With recent update (from Debian unstable), the dock interface remains named eth0, with udev debug I can see:

```
eth0: Policy *mac* yields "enx00*".
eth0: /usr/lib/udev/rules.d/80-net-setup-link.rules:11 NAME 'enx00*'
eth0: /usr/lib/udev/rules.d/99-systemd.rules:69 RUN '/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-sysctl --prefix=/net/ipv4/conf/$name --prefix=/net/ipv4/neigh/$
eth0: sd-device: Created database file '/run/udev/data/n9' for '/devices/pci0000:00/0000:00:1c.4/0000:02:00.0/0000:03:01.0/0000:05:00.0/0000:
eth0: Failed to rename network interface 9 from 'eth0' to 'enx00*': File exists
eth0: sd-device: Created database file '/run/udev/data/n9' for '/devices/pci0000:00/0000:00:1c.4/0000:02:00.0/0000:03:01.0/0000:05:00.0/0000:
eth0: Failed to process device, ignoring: File exists
```

Once I remove "mac" from the 99-default.link + rebuild initramfs, it works again.

Not sure if the source problem is elsewhere, but this regression causes real problems (iptables rules mapped to eth name stops working etc). And I cannot use different MAC fo dock due to department DHCP policy.


### Unexpected behaviour you saw

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce the problem

_No response_

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

_No response_
comments: I guess you use custom .link file for dock interface, right? Could you provide the file?

hmm, i wonder if for the netif of the dock the other en* names got so long that they didn't fit into the 15 avail chars anymore (simply because of a series of pci brigdes), and hence the enx* name ended up being the only one short enough, but that then collides because it is not as unique as it should be...

i wonder what the right approach here is: maybe we should not do mac-based renaming at all if the MAC address isnt the original one.

How did you do the MAC address cloning thing precisely?

I do not use any custom link file or config (unless it is hidden somewhere I forgot to check but /etc is clean and /usr is default install :-)

The MAC cloning is done by HW, I think I just set option in BIOS. Will check, but I am pretty sure this is option of Lenovo notebooks since USB-C/Thunderbolt docks were introuced.

ok, just checked - Lenovo BIOS (in config/network) has an option "MAC Address Pass Through" that is set to "internal MAC". It will set the attached dock ethernet interface to the same MAC as the internal interface.
debug level logs of udev + networkd is probably going to be useful to have

systemd-netword.service is disabled on this system (it uses networkmanager), what more you need from udev debug then I pasted above? (I enabled debug only for short time when attaching dock through USBC/Thunderbolt cable).

So, the firmware (or kernel) is borked in this case, as the persistent MAC address is shared by the two interfaces. When 'MAC Address Pass Through' is enabled, the `addr_assign_type` attribute of the dock interface should be `NET_ADDR_STOLEN`.

So, I think there is nothing we can do. And, unless such broken configuration in firmware is very common, we should not kill the feature. But, may be better to announce such 'Pass Through' feature is not supported in NEWS.
Sorry, but nothing borken except systemd. The internal inteface is disabled, when dock is attached. there is no two active intefaces with the same address.

hmm, so you are saying that at no point in time two interfaces exist with the same MAC address? i.e. that by the time the dock ethernet device shows up the laptop-internal one appears unplugged?

I guess we should make sure that if two netif devices share the same mac address for whatever weird reason we do something useful, i.e. just go for the next possible name in the list, gracefully.

Well, this function is on many docks/notebooks. So I cannot say for sure that it blocks traffic everywhere (I do not use internal eth at all in fact, as it requires adapter, so there is never active traffic - but the interface remains visible in system).

I think the logic is that you have one assigned MAC (and it does not matter if the connection is through dock or not) and company policy assigns IP to specific nb based on this (I have three docking stations but the MAC is always the same). There will be perhaps many crappy fw implementations of it, but in general, I think this is configuration that should be supported (morever, it works for years, well perhaps just because of some luck with settings :)

That said, I am really not sure what is the correct approach - keep MAC for the last detected adapter (that could be racy)? Definitely this is the case for USB-C and Thunderbolt docks (the advertises MAC passthrough even as a feature).
